anf_compare.notes: No published English was consulted; translated from the PG 70 Greek only.

bible_refs.note: Lemma Καὶ τέσσαρες πτέρυγες τῷ ἑνί = LXX Ezekiel 1:6 exactly.
Lemma Καὶ ἔσονται ἐπὶ τῶν ὀρέων ὡς περιστεραί = LXX Ezekiel 7:16 (which continues μελέτης, 'doves that moan', behind Cyril's 'song').
λαλοῦντες τὸ Χριστοῦ μυστήριον echoes λαλῆσαι τὸ μυστήριον τοῦ Χριστοῦ.

Lemma Καὶ ἐὰν ὦσιν οἱ τρεῖς ἄνδρες οὗτοι ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῆς, Νωε καὶ Δανιηλ καὶ Ιωβ = LXX 14:14; 'saved by their own righteousness' renders the same verse's αὐτοὶ ἐν τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ αὐτῶν σωθήσονται (the triad recurs at 14:20).

choices.why: Cyril's usual name for the angelic orders; 'intellectual' misleads in modern English, and ἄνω means 'on high', not 'upper'.

choices.english: they do not sink down toward baser things
choices.why: ὀκλάζω is to crouch or bend the knee; set against standing it means sinking, and the negation is kept.
rejected: not crouching toward the more shameful

choices.term: οἶμαι δεῖν οὐκ ἀβασανίστους ἐᾷν τὰς τοῦ προφήτου φωνάς
choices.english: I think we must not leave the prophet's words unexamined
choices.why: ἀβασάνιστος is 'untested'; with the negation the sense is that the words must be examined.
rejected: I think it needful not to let the prophet's voices be untortured

choices.why: ψῆφος here is the judicial verdict, not a ballot.

pass_a_gloss: Heading: Fragments on Ezekiel; fragments from the catenae on Ezekiel. Lemma: and four wings to the one [Ezekiel 1:6]. [Cat. Ezech. f. 12b] For they stand always somehow, the intellectual (νοεραί) and above powers, not crouching (ὀκλάζουσαι) toward the baser things, but the straight and blameless path of the life fitting to them they dart along (διᾴττουσιν). Lemma: and they will be on the mountains as doves [Ezekiel 7:16]. [Cat. 18b] The blessed disciples; for they went around all under heaven, the mystery of Christ speaking, and as song and lyre having it. Lemma: and if these three men be in its midst, Noah and Daniel and Job [Ezekiel 14:14]. [Cat. f. 203b] Since I think it needful not to leave untested (ἀβασανίστους) the voices of the prophet, come, let us say why ever, Noah and Job and Daniel having died already, [PG 70.1460] and perhaps somewhere also of Daniel himself, he says them to be going to be saved in their own righteousness (δικαιοσύνῃ), and yet all the rest of the land, against which the vote (ψῆφος) of death might be brought out, being utterly destroyed.
pass_b_english: Fragments from the Catenae on Ezekiel.

“And four wings for each one” (Ezekiel 1:6). For in a sense the rational powers on high always stand: they do not sink down toward baser things, but speed along the straight and blameless path of the life that befits them.

“And they shall be on the mountains like doves” (Ezekiel 7:16). These are the blessed disciples. For they went about all the earth under heaven, speaking the mystery of Christ (Colossians 4:3), and they had it as their song and their lyre.

“And if these three men, Noah and Daniel and Job, are in its midst” (Ezekiel 14:14). Since I think we must not leave the prophet’s words unexamined, come, let us say why it is that, when Noah and Job and Daniel were already dead (and perhaps even Daniel himself), he says that they will be saved by their own righteousness (Ezekiel 14:14), even though all the rest of the land, against which the sentence of death might be pronounced, is being destroyed.
source_text:
Fragmenta in Ezechielem
FRAGMENTA EX CATENIS IN EZECHIELEM
Καὶ τέσσαρες πτέρυγες τῷ ἑνί. Cat. Ezech. f. 12. b. Ἑστήκασι γὰρ ἀεί πως αἱ
νοεραὶ καὶ ἄνω δυνάμεις, οὐκ ὀκλάζουσαι πρὸς τὰ αἰσχίω, ἀλλὰ τὴν ὀρθὴν καὶ
ἀμώμητον τῆς αὐταῖς πρεπούσης ζωῆς διᾴττουσιν τρίβον. Καὶ ἔσονται ἐπὶ τῶν
ὀρέων ὡς περιστεραί. Cat. 18.b. Οἱ μακάριοι μαθηταί· περιῆλθον γὰρ πᾶσαν ὑπ'
οὐρανὸν, τὸ Χριστοῦ λαλοῦντες μυστήριον, καὶ ᾠδὴν καὶ λύραν ἔχοντες αὐτό. Καὶ
ἐὰν ὦσιν οἱ τρεῖς ἄνδρες οὗτοι ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῆς, Νῶε, καὶ ∆ανιὴλ, καὶ Ἰώβ. Cat. f.
203. b.Ἐπειδὴ οἶμαι δεῖν οὐκ ἀβασανίστους ἐᾷν τὰς τοῦ προφήτου φωνὰς, φέρε
λέγωμεν τί δήποτε, Νῶε καὶ Ἰὼβ καὶ ∆ανιὴλ τεθνεώτων ἤδη, 70.1460 τάχα δέ που
καὶ αὐτοῦ τοῦ ∆ανιὴλ, σωθήσεσθαί φησιν αὐτοὺς ἐν τῇ ἰδίᾳ δικαιοσύνῃ, καί τοι τῆς
ἄλλης ἁπάσης γῆς, καθ' ἧς ἂν ἡ τοῦ θανάτου ψῆφος ἐκφέροιτο, καταφθειρομένης.
reviewer: claude (Wave A review, clause by clause against the Greek)
review_notes: Replaces a scaffold row that held no translation; the English is new, translated from the locked PG 70 Greek in translations/fe_frag_open_source.json.
Reviewer change: word order only ('in a sense ... always stand' for ἀεί πως).
Lemmas checked against LXX Ezekiel 1:6, 7:16 and 14:14; Colossians 4:3 checked.
The doubled Daniel in the list of the dead is kept as printed and explained in the translator notes; no emendation.
Negations kept: 'do not sink down', 'must not leave ... unexamined'.
